fullPassage: We often associate the concept of temperature with how hot or cold an object feels when we touch it. In this way, our senses provide us with a qualitative indication of temperature. Our senses, however, are unreliable and often mislead us. For example, if you stand in bare feet with one foot on carpet and the other on a tile floor, the tile feels colder than the carpet even though both are at the same temperature. The two objects feel different because tile transfers energy by heat at a higher rate than carpet does. Your skin "measures" the rate of energy transfer by heat rather than the actual temperature. What we need is a reliable and reproducible method for measuring the relative hotness or coldness of objects rather than the rate of energy transfer. Scientists have developed a variety of thermometers for making such quantitative measurements.

det.korean: thermometer=온도계 (온도를 측정하는 데 쓰이는 기구)
det.analysis:
❌ ① concept(개념): 생각으로 정의와 다름
❌ ② indication(지표): 나타내는 신호로 정의와 다름
❌ ③ variety(다양성): 종류로 정의와 무관
✅ ④ thermometer(온도계): 온도를 측정하는 기구로 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: thermometer = 온도계. instrument for measuring temperature가 핵심 단서

questions.passage: What we need is a reliable method for measuring hotness or coldness. Scientists have __________ (development) a variety of thermometers for making such quantitative measurements.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: have + 과거분사 developed: 현재완료 '개발해 왔다'
det.analysis: 'Scientists have __________ a variety of thermometers'에서 have 뒤에 현재완료를 이루는 과거분사가 필요하다. 명사 development(개발)를 동사 develop의 과거분사 developed로 바꾼다. development → developed
det.tip: have + p.p.(현재완료): have developed(개발해 왔다)

questions.passage: The two objects feel different because tile transfers energy by heat at a __________ (high) rate than carpet does. Your skin "measures" the rate of energy transfer by heat rather than the actual temperature.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: than과 함께 쓰이는 비교급 higher (형용사 high → 비교급 higher)
det.analysis: 'at a __________ rate than carpet does'에서 뒤에 than이 있으므로 비교급이 필요하다. 형용사 high를 비교급 higher로 바꾼다. high → higher
det.tip: 비교급 + than: at a higher rate than ~

questions.passage: We often associate the concept of temperature with how hot or cold an object feels when we touch it. In this way, our senses provide us with __________. Our senses, however, are unreliable and often mislead us. For example, if you stand in bare feet with one foot on carpet and the other on a tile floor, the tile feels colder than the carpet even though both are at the same temperature. The two objects feel different because tile transfers energy by heat at a higher rate than carpet does. Your skin "measures" the rate of energy transfer by heat rather than the actual temperature. What we need is a reliable and reproducible method for measuring the relative hotness or coldness of objects rather than the rate of energy transfer. Scientists have developed a variety of thermometers for making such quantitative measurements.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: a qualitative indication of temperature=온도에 대한 정성적 지표 — 감각이 주는 것
det.analysis:
❌ ① a precise numerical value of temperature(정확한 수치): 감각은 숫자가 아닌 느낌을 주며, 뒤에서 감각이 신뢰할 수 없다고 함
✅ ② a qualitative indication of temperature(온도에 대한 정성적 지표): 감각이 온도에 대한 정성적(주관적) 지표를 준다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ a complete map of the whole room(방 전체의 지도): 본문과 무관
❌ ④ a permanent record of the weather(날씨 기록): 본문과 무관
det.tip: our senses provide us with a qualitative indication of temperature

ch: a precise numerical value of temperature
a complete map of the whole room
a permanent record of the weather

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: the rate of energy transfer by heat rather than the actual temperature=실제 온도가 아니라 열 전달 속도 — 피부가 실제로 재는 것
det.analysis:
